subject: English
passage: Layla Hassan employed the pseudonym "Zhuangzi"—the name of an ancient Chinese philosopher—in literary criticism essays she wrote in 1872, a choice that accomplished far more than simply concealing her authorship. ______ it wasn't an arbitrary pen name but rather a complex rhetorical strategy through which Hassan aligned her aesthetic views with the venerated Daoist principles of the classical era, thereby bolstering the authority of her writing.
prompt: Which choice completes the text with the most logical transition?
explanation: Choice D is the best answer. The first sentence claims Hassan's pseudonym choice 'accomplished far more than simply concealing her authorship,' creating an expectation that the following sentence will explain this additional significance. 'Indeed' provides the most logical transition by signaling emphatic confirmation—the second sentence validates and specifies the complexity hinted at in the first by revealing the pseudonym was 'a complex rhetorical strategy' aligning her views with Daoist principles. This relationship makes 'Indeed' the appropriate connector.
